problem.text: Sidorenko's conjecture in the homomorphism-density form t(H, G) >= p(G)^{e(H)} for every bipartite H with an edge, and the forcing conjecture of Skokan-Thoma and Conlon-Fox-Sudakov (every bipartite graph with a cycle is forcing).

claims.text: Theorem 1.1: the incidence graph H of the 22 triples on 13 points (35 vertices, 66 edges) satisfies t(H, G) < p(G)^66 for some finite simple G. Corollary 1.2: t(H, F)/p(F)^66 can be made arbitrarily small, and blow-ups give an injective-copy deficit at one positive limiting density. Corollary 1.3: H is not p-forcing at one density p, so the forcing conjecture fails.

assumptions.text: Lemma 3.1, proved in Sections 4-7 with D = 2r fixed above explicit thresholds before q tends to infinity; the four finite properties of Proposition 2.1 of the fixed complex; Lemma 4.6 uses point degree at most 6 and D >= 12; Proposition 7.7 uses D > 1641.

methods.text: A nonnegative kernel built from signed rank-r layers of symmetric matrix differences over F_q, one coordinate per incidence; activation laws with signed overlap moments; a coordinate expansion in which the only nonconstant contributions come from point pairs whose two faces are both active (the four-incidence parity); one negative term at the identity type assignment; type pinning by colour-refinement scores; dilution and a crossed product to a symmetric kernel; independent sampling to a finite simple host; Lagrangian intersection counts and profile costs for singular configurations.

evidence.text: Complete proofs in the manuscript; the finite properties of the complex are certified from Tables 1 and 2. The openai/math catalogue lists a Lean formalization of the Sidorenko statement (lean/docs/161.md); this record has not run it. This record's probe complex-structure-1 rechecked the combinatorial properties of Table 1 and found the complex to be a triangulated 2-sphere whose three bit positions are the sides of three Hamiltonian cycles.

limitations.text: The host is only shown to exist; the forcing consequence is proved at one density; the construction is carried out for this one complex and is not stated for other patterns; the manuscript does not describe the complex as a sphere; it is an AI-produced preprint without peer review, and the record has not verified the analytic estimates of Sections 4-7 line by line.

relevance.text: Decisive source after 2026-09-23. As this record reads Equation (3.4) and Lemma 3.4, the construction's correction comes only from point pairs that lie in two faces, that is, from 4-cycles of H, and the pinning step needs discrete colour refinement, which never holds for a biregular graph. These two facts delimit which bipartite graphs the construction can reach and motivate the candidate questions of this exploration.
